name: Cao Jisheng
current_role: Chairman and Party Secretary, Shandong Yisheng Livestock & Poultry Breeding Co. (002458.SZ)
profile: Cao Jisheng (b. 1960), an MBA and senior veterinarian from Yantai, Shandong, co-founded Yisheng with 33 others in 1997 and built it into China's major supplier of grandparent/parent-stock white-feather broiler breeders and breeding pigs; it listed in Shenzhen in 2010. He has chaired it since then and holds about 41% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Yisheng co-founded by Cao with 33 other people in 1997 in Yantai; it is now one of China's key suppliers of high-generation poultry breeding stock and was named a national pig core breeding farm.
deep_cut_fact: Cao is a qualified senior veterinarian (高级兽医师) and serves as president of the China Animal Agriculture Association's white-feather broiler branch and of the Shandong Animal Husbandry Association; he is also a deputy to the 14th Shandong Provincial People's Congress.
notes: Low international profile; best route is the board office (董事会办公室) IR email; Chinese-language outreach advised. Company email/website as listed in exchange-filing data (Eastmoney F10).

name: Gary E. Dickerson
current_role: President and CEO, Applied Materials (AMAT)
profile: Gary Dickerson has led Applied Materials, the world's largest semiconductor equipment maker, as CEO since 2013 after joining as president in 2012. He spent 18 years at KLA-Tencor (rising to president/COO) and seven years as CEO of Varian Semiconductor, which he sold to Applied for $4.9bn in 2011. His wealth is AMAT stock; Applied is now riding AI-driven chip demand.
interesting_fact: Under Dickerson Applied is investing up to $4bn in the EPIC Center in Silicon Valley, a collaborative R&D hub for chipmakers and universities; in Q3 FY2026 Applied posted record revenue of $9.12bn.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in manufacturing and engineering management at General Motors' Delco Electronics division and AT&T Technologies, after a B.S. in engineering management from the University of Missouri-Rolla; in 2024 Singapore awarded him its Public Service Star.
notes: Press releases list Ricky Gradwohl (editorial/media) and Mike Sullivan (financial community) as company contacts (phone only, no email found). Natural fit for a data-center/AI-chip episode; route via Applied corporate communications.

name: Bao Xiaojun
current_role: Chairman, President and core technical staff, Guangdong Naruida Technology (688522.SH, Zhuhai)
profile: Bao Xiaojun (XIAOJUN BAO, b. 1973, master's degree) founded Zhuhai Naruida in 2014 after engineering stints in North America, and built it into a maker of full-polarization active phased-array radars for weather detection and low-altitude/'low-slow-small' target surveillance. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market; his Hurun fortune is shared with Liu Suling.
interesting_fact: Naruida pairs phased-array with dual-polarization technology to make advanced radar cheap enough for civilian weather networks; its products won gold at the 10th and 11th World Radar Expo.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Naruida, Bao worked as an engineer at Raytheon in Canada (2006-2013) and then briefly at AMD (2013-2014), founding the company in May 2014.
notes: Technical founder with North American career (likely English-capable). Low-altitude economy/radar angle. Contact via IR email (board secretary 龚雪华).

name: Lv Dongfang
current_role: Director and General Manager, Heilongjiang Tianyouwei Electronics (603202.SH)
profile: Lv Dongfang (b. 1973) co-built Tianyouwei, a Suihua, Heilongjiang maker of automotive instrument clusters that is expanding into smart cockpits, with subsidiaries in Liuzhou, Wuhan and Mexico. She has been general manager since 2022; the company listed in Shanghai in 2025. Her Hurun fortune is shared with chairman Wang Wenbo.
interesting_fact: Lv Dongfang is a deputy to China's 14th National People's Congress.
deep_cut_fact: She has been with the business from the start: in 2001-2003 she was director and executive deputy GM of its predecessor, Harbin Tianyouwei Electronic Instrument Manufacturing Co., before the company moved to Suihua in 2003.
notes: Contact via securities department (证券部) email; board secretary 张智. Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Que Weidong
current_role: General Manager and Director, Quechen Silicon Chemical Co. (605183.SH, Wuxi); previously also chairman
profile: Que Weidong (b. 1968, master's degree) founded Quechen Silicon Chemical in Wuxi in 2003 and built a fully integrated chain from sulfuric acid and sodium silicate to precipitated silica, becoming a leading maker of highly dispersible silica for 'green' low-rolling-resistance tyres. Quechen listed in Shanghai in December 2020; he remains general manager.
interesting_fact: Quechen is described as one of the world's main producers of highly dispersible silica for green tyres, and its technology won a China Petroleum & Chemical Industry Federation science & technology progress award.
deep_cut_fact: Que has run Quechen as general manager without a break since January 2003, the month the company was founded in Donggang town, Xishan district, Wuxi.
notes: Chairmanship now held by 陈小燕; Que is GM. Contact via IR email (board secretary 任海燕).

name: Chen Jianping
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Jame Technology Corp. (300868.SZ)
profile: Chen Jianping (b. 1983) co-founded Shenzhen Jame Technology in 2009, a designer and maker of mobile-phone cases and protective accessories for major handset brands and its own brands. He has chaired it since 2013; Jame listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2020. His Hurun fortune is shared with Yang Meihua.
interesting_fact: Chen made the Hurun China Under-40 self-made rich list in 2020, the year Jame went public, with only a technical secondary-school (zhongzhuan) education.
deep_cut_fact: Before Jame he was director and GM of Shenzhen Jiameng Technology and executive director of Shenzhen Shenghuohui Trading; at Jame itself he started as supervisor (2009-2013) before becoming chairman.
notes: Hurun U40 source is the input metadata (Hurun China U40 2020); education per company filing. Contact via IR (board secretary 周波).

name: Dong Yu
current_role: Director, Cubic Sensor and Instrument Co. (688665.SH, Wuhan); chairman of Wuhan Dashan Precision Furnace; GM of Youhui Investment
profile: Dong Yu (b. 1971) is a director and major holder of Cubic Sensor and Instrument, a Wuhan maker of gas sensors and gas-analysis instruments founded and chaired by Xiong Youhui, with whom her Hurun fortune is shared. Cubic listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021; she also chairs Wuhan Dashan Precision Furnace and runs Youhui Investment.
interesting_fact: Cubic's gas sensors go into air purifiers, HVAC, cars and smart meters, and the company drafts industry standards in gas sensing; it grew out of the Huazhong University of Science and Technology research ecosystem.
deep_cut_fact: Dong trained as a doctor: she graduated in clinical medicine from Tongji Medical University and worked as staff at Huazhong University of Science and Technology from 2000 to 2013 before moving into business.
notes: Female per company filings. Non-executive role; Xiong Youhui is the operating founder. Contact via board office email.

name: Cao Guowei (Charles Chao)
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Weibo Corporation (NASDAQ: WB / HKEX: 9898); director of SINA
profile: Shanghai-born Charles Chao joined Sina in 1999 as VP finance and rose to CFO, president, CEO (2006) and chairman (2012-2021), green-lighting the launch of Sina Weibo in 2009. He chairs Weibo, China's leading microblogging platform, and led Sina's 2021 take-private via his vehicle New Wave. Wealth comes from Weibo/Sina stakes.
interesting_fact: Chao is credited with backing the 2009 launch of Sina Weibo, which became China's dominant public social-media platform and listed on Nasdaq in 2014 and in Hong Kong in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: He started as a journalist: a Fudan journalism graduate and news correspondent, he took a journalism MA at the University of Oklahoma, then switched to accounting at UT Austin and became an audit manager at PwC before joining Sina.
notes: Stepped down as Sina chairman in March 2021 but remains a director; still Weibo chairman per 2026 AGM. The Weibo handle @来去之间 belongs to Weibo CEO Wang Gaofei, not Chao. Birth year conflicts (1961 vs 1965) in sources.

name: Wang Qiangzhong
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Best (百斯特) Investment Group; co-founder and shareholder of CoCreation Grass (605099.SH)
profile: Wang Qiangzhong (b. 1962, Huai'an, Jiangsu) started out making school teaching aids and founded CoCreation Grass, now a leading global artificial-turf maker and Huai'an's first home-grown listed private company (chaired by Wang Qiangxiang). He now chairs Jiangsu Best Investment Group, building a 'seed-to-chopsticks' food chain, and is a 13th/14th National People's Congress deputy.
interesting_fact: He is a deputy to China's 13th and 14th National People's Congress and has received the National May Day Labour Medal and Jiangsu Model Worker title.
deep_cut_fact: A native of Shihe town in Huai'an district, he trained in electronics at Huaiyin Industrial School (1986) and serves as honorary 'town mayor' of the Shihe Smart Education town, promoting a 'New Shihe + AI + teaching equipment' model for the local teaching-aids industry.
notes: Holds ~2.4% of CoCreation Grass directly (Q3 2026), with Jiangsu Best Investment holding ~15.8%; the listed company's chairman is Wang Qiangxiang. IR email reaches CoCreation, not Best Group.

name: Wang Juan
current_role: Chairwoman, Suzhou Shijia Science & Technology Inc. (002796.SZ)
profile: Wang Juan (b. 1966) built Suzhou Shijia from an elevator-decoration workshop into a precision sheet-metal and die-casting group making elevator car systems and equipment enclosures, plus mobile-communications components and medical consumables, with a plant in Malaysia. She has chaired the company since its 2011 conversion; it listed in Shenzhen in May 2016.
interesting_fact: Shijia's core precision-enclosure business makes elevator car (cab) systems, and it has diversified into telecom base-station equipment and medical consumables, including a Malaysian subsidiary.
deep_cut_fact: Her career began in 1997 at the Suzhou Shijia Elevator Decoration Factory (世嘉电梯装饰装潢厂), the forerunner of today's listed company; she later chaired Shijia Medical Technology and its Malaysian unit, Shijia Technologies (M) Sdn. Bhd.
notes: Holds Canadian permanent residency per filings. Appeared on Hurun China only in 2016. Contact via board office email (secretary 康云华).

KWG, listed in Hong Kong since 2007, spans residential development, property services and commercial operations, hotels, cultural tourism, education and healthcare.

name: Jeremy Simmons Spivey
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Cardinal Infrastructure Group Inc. (NASDAQ: CDNL), Raleigh, NC
profile: Jeremy Spivey founded Cardinal in Raleigh in 2013 as a niche wet-utilities (water, sewer, stormwater) installer and grew it, partly via acquisitions, into a full-service site-infrastructure contractor across Raleigh, Charlotte and Greensboro, now expanding to Florida (Hughes Brothers deal, $357.5m). Cardinal IPO'd on Nasdaq; Q3 2026 revenue rose 65% to $201.9m.
interesting_fact: Cardinal is buying Central Florida heavy-civil contractor Hughes Brothers Construction for $357.5 million (announced Oct 2026), its first big move outside North Carolina.
deep_cut_fact: Spivey began his career on a utility crew and worked his way through every core part of the business over 30+ years; he holds a B.S. in Construction Management with a business minor from East Carolina University.
notes: Recent IPO; board includes Hosted Solutions data-center founder (Mr. Lee) — possible data-center-site-work angle. Q3 2026 margins disappointed, so avoid leading with stock performance.

name: Institut Fur Marktentscheidungen e.V. Nurnberg (NIM – Nuremberg Institute for Market Decisions)
current_role: Non-profit association; >10% shareholder of NIQ Global Intelligence plc (NYSE: NIQ). President: Ralf Klein-Bölting
profile: NIM is the Nuremberg non-profit association (e.V.) that founded GfK in 1934 and now conducts behavioural and market-decision research (incl. the long-running GfK/NIM Consumer Climate index). After NIQ (NielsenIQ) acquired GfK in 2023, NIM became a major NIQ shareholder, holding >10% after NIQ's 2025 IPO. Not a person.
interesting_fact: GfK was founded in 1934 by Nuremberg university lecturers including future German Economics Minister and Chancellor Ludwig Erhard, with the concept developed by Wilhelm Vershofen.
deep_cut_fact: NIM's executive board explicitly lists its role as a NielsenIQ shareholder among its duties, and a Members' Council of business leaders must approve decisions on that stake; NIM also publishes the NIM Marketing Intelligence Review and runs 'Voices of the Leaders of Tomorrow' studies.
notes: Institutional holder, not an individual: an interview would be with NIM's president (Ralf Klein-Bölting) or researchers (e.g. consumer-climate head Rolf Bürkl). 'alive' not applicable.
